method: Inspected restored 4-fps full-shot contact sheets, selected full-resolution frames, and dense consecutive-frame face crops around find / So / paid / stop it and P01a tail. Created exact 220-frame two-part diagnostic preview and verified 1x browser playback reaches the end. No continuous audiovisual human perception is claimed from browser screenshots.
review_limitations: Mouth aperture correlations and onset counts are weak diagnostics. Word transcript times are approximate and are not phoneme alignments. Dense samples support visual mouth-shape observations, not a certified perceptual sync pass. Browser playback evidence establishes successful 1x playback, not uninterrupted audiovisual listening. Preserve the flags pending direct perceptual review; no batch clearance.
observations: Identity, wardrobe, glasses, room, camera and resting hands are stable in reviewed samples. No obvious hand/face deformation was found.

Source frames 17–32 show a rounded shape consistent with So, but the mouth is already active around narration-relative .278–.403 s, before the detected .42 s speech onset. This is a timing concern, not proof, since preparatory movement can lead speech.

Source frames 106–107 show a clear lip closure, followed by release/opening at 108–109. Relative to the approximate paid start at narration 4.183 s, the closure is about .16–.20 s early and release about .07–.11 s early. This is suggestive of anticipation; word boundary uncertainty prevents treating it as a precise phoneme offset.

Source frames 120–131 around stop it show closure at 121–122, reopening at 123–127, and a settled closed mouth by 128–130. The sequence is plausible, but direct audiovisual review is required to assess perceived timing.
Both diagnostic signals fail: narration correlation .483 versus guide .501; only 1 of 2 onsets matched at −7.93 frames. No automatic sync pass is supported.
